name: Palor
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: D'Alton, Paula 1987. Le Palor: esquisse phonologique et grammaticale d'une langue cangin du Senegal. Paris: CNRS; also Merrill 2023, The Cangin Languages (Brill), paywalled
earlier_scan.note: Full phonological sketch exists (D'Alton 1987) but no online copy located; Merrill 2023 Brill volume also plausibly covers Palor prosody.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE inventory 1324 'Ndut-Falor' (source: Pichl 1973), phoible.org/inventories/view/1324; Glottolog 5.3 languoid page palo1243; WALS languoid plr (source D'Alton 1983); WALS CLDF.
sources.note: PHOIBLE lists 43 segments and no stress or tone marks; WALS has five values for Palor (63A, 117A-120A), none for stress features 14A-16A; Glottolog lists no further descriptive works beyond those above plus Cissé 2010 (MA thesis on the simple sentence, UCAD, not located) and Pichl 1966 (restricted handle 11858/00-001M-0000-0012-9603-5).

sources.citation: Zuk, Fabian. 2024. Merrill, John T. M., The Cangin languages [review]. Linguistique et langues africaines 10(2). doi:10.4000/13lt8.
sources.note: Review read via download tool at journals.openedition.org/lla/14025: it discusses consonant/vowel reconstruction and morphology and says nothing about stress, accent or prosody; PDF download (hal.science/hal-05015217) blocked by Anubis bot-wall so no file.

sources.citation: Merrill, John T. M. 2018. The historical origin of consonant mutation in the Atlantic languages. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. 489 pp.
sources.note: Uses Palor data from D'Alton 1983 for root-final consonant alternations (p. 40, ex. 25) and Proto-Cangin reconstruction (ch. 7 fn. 156, App. C); a full-text search for stress/accent full text finds no statement about stress or accent in Palor or any Cangin language.

sources.citation: Drolc, Ursula. 2006. L'évolution du système consonantique des langues cangin. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online (AAeO) 2006, doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2006_3513.
sources.note: Comparative consonant study (26 pp., text). Only 'accent' mention is generic (printed p. 4, para <11>: sound change can depend on 'la place de l'accent'); nothing on Palor stress.

sources.citation: Thornell, Christina. 2016. Grammaire de base sur la langue paloor au Sénégal. Dakar: ASPAD/SIL. 174 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recent SIL/ASPAD basic grammar of Paloor; a basic grammar usually opens with a phonology-and-orthography section that may mention accent. SIL archive pages blocked (not reachable by automated download).

tone.summary: Basic grammar with a phonology chapter (20 vowels with length and ATR contrasts, 27 consonants, CV/CVC syllables); says nothing about tone, pitch or word stress; the acute accent marks +ATR vowels.
tone.citation_as_reported: Thornell, Christina (avec Marie Diouf, Mamadou Diouf, Ibrahima Ciss, Abdoulaye Diouf et Fatou Diouf). 2016. Grammaire de base sur la langue paloor au Senegal. Goteborg / Dakar: SIL & ASPAD (Association des Paloor pour le Developpement). 172 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 80257.

sources.citation: Merrill, John T. M. 2023. The Cangin Languages: Phonological and Morphological Reconstruction and Diachrony. Leiden: Brill. Ch. 2 'Phonology', pp. 16-90.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative-historical monograph; most recent expert treatment of Cangin phonology covering Palor, likely to state the (Proto-)Cangin stress pattern and Palor specifics. Google Books preview exists (id 2ur7EAAAQBAJ) but is CAPTCHA-could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Soukka, Maria & Heikki Soukka. 2011. Esquisses phonologiques du laalaa et palor (langues cangin du Sénégal). Göteborg Africana Informal Series 8; Dakar: SIL.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: A dedicated phonological sketch of Palor (with Laalaa) by SIL Senegal linguists; almost certainly has a suprasegmentals section. Not found in GUPEA or via SIL's could not be reached by automated download archive search; may be in SIL Language & Culture Archives.
sources.venue: Göteborg Africana Informal Series 8; Dakar: SIL

sources.note: The primary modern phonological+grammatical description of Palor; its phonology chapter is the most likely home of an explicit accent statement. HathiTrust search-only copy could at least give page hits for 'accent' from a browser; Harvard print copy is(a scan can be requested through your own library).

sources.note: First description of the Cangin group including Palor; older and less reliable (Merrill notes inaccuracies in Pichl's data) but may carry an early accent remark.

sources.citation: Pichl, Walter J. 1980. Ndut-Falor. In M. E. Kropp Dakubu (ed.), West African Language Data Sheets, vol. 2, pp. 159-166. [Accra]: West African Linguistic Society / Leiden: African Studies Centre. (PHOIBLE source 1324_fap dates it '1973'.)

sources.access_detail: in print; a research-library copy was located; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: WALDS data sheets follow a fixed questionnaire whose phonology block includes a line for tones/stress, so this 8-page sheet is the most likely place for an early explicit statement on whether Ndut-Falor has tone; PHOIBLE's transcription of it (GM 1324) records 43 segments and no tonemes. Not seen: print only, no scan located (archive.org search for the WALDS volumes: 0 hits; HathiTrust bot-walled by automated download).
